uncited: Real-time KD Tree Construction is a technique for building k-d tree spatial partitioning structures on the GPU to enable immediate use in rendering pipelines, specifically addressing the latency of traditional CPU-based construction.

It sets itself apart from its parent method, [K-D Tree Hierarchy Construction](2300-k-d-tree-hierarchy-construction.md), by utilizing GPU parallelism and breadth-first search (BFS) to achieve real-time performance, whereas the parent implies a general hierarchical construction often assumed to be offline or CPU-bound.
It differs from [GPU K-D Tree Ray Traversal](4575-gpu-k-d-tree-ray-traversal.md) by focusing on the *construction* phase rather than the *traversal* phase.

The specific memory layout is not detailed in the provided sources, but the structure follows the standard k-d tree node definition implied by the parent article: a split plane (axis and position) and child node indices.
It is chosen when dealing with sparse volumetric data where traditional partitioning methods are inefficient.
It was developed to address the need for real-time spatial partitioning in rendering applications, moving away from offline CPU-based construction.
